statement: The circles $x^{2}+y^{2}=25$ and $(x-3)^{2}+y^{2}=16$ intersect. Find the equation of their common chord and the points of intersection.
solution: Expand the second: $x^{2}-6x+9+y^{2}=16\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}=6x+7$. Subtract from the first: $25-(6x+7)=0\Rightarrow 18-6x=0\Rightarrow x=3$. So the common chord is the line $x=3$. Substituting into $x^{2}+y^{2}=25$ gives $9+y^{2}=25$, so $y=\pm 4$. The intersections are $(3,4)$ and $(3,-4)$.
hints: Subtract the two circle equations to eliminate $x^{2}+y^{2}$.
Substitute the resulting line back into a circle.
